'''Hongjie Dai''' ({{lang-zh|c=戴宏杰}}; born 2 May 1966 in [[Shaoyang]], [[China]])<ref name="mosher">{{citation|url=http://library.stanford.edu/depts/swain/history/mosher/biography.html |title=Stanford Chemistry Department History 1977 to 2000. VI. Professors, Brief Biographical Summaries 1976–2000 |first=Harry S. |last=Mosher |publisher=Stanford University Library |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120212205847/http://library.stanford.edu/depts/swain/history/mosher/biography.html |archivedate=12 February 2012 }}.</ref> is a Chinese–American nanotechnologist, applied physicist, and chemist. He is the Sapientia Eminence Professor at the [[University of Hong Kong]] and the J.G. Jackson & C.J. Wood Professor of Chemistry at [[Stanford University]].<ref name="suchem">{{cite web|title=Chemistry Faculty: Faculty Research Interests - Hongjie Dai|url=http://www.stanford.edu/dept/chemistry/faculty/dai/|publisher=Stanford University|accessdate=9 June 2010}}.</ref> A leading figure in the study of [[carbon nanotubes]],<ref>{{citation|title=A Wisp of Carbon, a Whiff of Gases|first=Anne|last=Eisenberg|date=2 March 2000|journal=[[The New York Times]]|url=https://select.nytimes.com/gst/abstract.html?res=FB0A12F93B5D0C718CDDAA0894D8404482}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Researchers Develop First Integrated Silicon Circuit With Nanotube Transistors|journal=ScienceDaily|date=7 January 2004|url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2004/01/040107072303.htm}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Nanotubes smuggle anti-HIV molecules into cells
|date=21 February 2007|first=Celeste|last=Biever|journal=[[New Scientist]]|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/dn11226-nanotubes-smuggle-antihiv-molecules-into-cells.html}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Nanotubes cut to ribbons: New techniques open up carbon tubes to create ribbons|first=Geoff|last=Brumfiel|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|date=15 April 2009|doi=10.1038/news.2009.367}}.</ref> Dai is ranked as one of the top chemists in the world by Science Watch.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Top 100 Chemists, 2000-2010|url = http://archive.sciencewatch.com/dr/sci/misc/Top100Chemists2000-10/|website = ScienceWatch |access-date = 2016-01-31}}</ref> He is currently the scientific advisor and co-founder to Nirmidas Biotech, Inc., which aims to commercialize his breakthrough research on NIR-II dyes and plasmonic gold (pGOLD) to applications in healthcare and in vitro diagnostics.

Dai received a B.S. in physics from [[Tsinghua University]] in 1989, then went to the United States through the [[CUSPEA]] program organized by Prof. [[T. D. Lee]]. He finished an M.S. in applied sciences from [[Columbia University]] in 1991, and a PhD in applied physics from [[Harvard University]] in 1994 under the direction of Prof. [[Charles Lieber]]. After [[postdoctoral research]] at Harvard, he joined the Stanford faculty as an assistant professor in 1997.<ref name="mosher"/><ref name="suchem"/> In 2024, Dai joined the [[University of Hong Kong]] as a joint Professor of department of chemistry and department of mechanical engineering.

Among his awards are the [[American Chemical Society]]'s [[ACS Award in pure chemistry]], 2002,<ref name="suchem"/><ref>[http://portal.acs.org/portal/acs/corg/content?_nfpb=true&_pageLabel=PP_ARTICLEMAIN&node_id=1319&content_id=CTP_004546&use_sec=true&sec_url_var=region1&__uuid=33df65a1-6741-4e5d-803c-05134255c9ed ACS Award in Pure Chemistry] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120323220419/http://portal.acs.org/portal/acs/corg/content?_nfpb=true&_pageLabel=PP_ARTICLEMAIN&node_id=1319&content_id=CTP_004546&use_sec=true&sec_url_var=region1&__uuid=33df65a1-6741-4e5d-803c-05134255c9ed |date=23 March 2012 }}, American Chemical Society, retrieved 2011-04-09.</ref> the Julius Springer Prize for Applied Physics, 2004,<ref name="suchem"/><ref>{{citation|title=Julius Springer Prize for Applied Physics 2004 awarded|publisher=Springer-Verlag|date=5 October 2004|url=https://www.springer.com/about+springer/media/pressreleases?SGWID=0-11002-6-803600-0}}.</ref> and the [[American Physical Society]]'s [[James C. McGroddy Prize for New Materials]], 2006.<ref name="suchem"/><ref>{{citation|title=2006 James C. McGroddy Prize for New Materials Recipient |url=http://www.americanphysicalsociety.com/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Hongjie&last_nm=Dai&year=2006 |publisher=American Physical Society |accessdate=2011-04-09 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110903222812/http://www.americanphysicalsociety.com/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Hongjie&last_nm=Dai&year=2006 |archivedate=3 September 2011}}.</ref> He was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2009, and to the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2011.<ref name="suchem"/><ref>{{citation|title=11 Stanford faculty inducted into AAAS |journal=Stanford Daily |date=23 April 2009 |url=http://www.stanforddaily.com/2009/04/23/brief-11-stanford-faculty-inducted-into-aaas/ }}{{dead link|date=April 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Three Stanford scholars tapped as AAAS fellows|journal=Stanford Report|date=12 January 2011|url=http://news.stanford.edu/news/2011/january/aaas-science-fellow-011211.html}}.</ref> He was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2016,<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-3-2016-NAS-Election.html|title=National Academy of Sciences Members and Foreign Associates Elected|department=News from the National Academy of Sciences|publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]]|date=3 May 2016|accessdate=2016-05-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160506052951/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-3-2016-NAS-Election.html|archive-date=6 May 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> and in 2019 he was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Medicine]]<ref>{{citation|url=https://nam.edu/national-academy-of-medicine-elects-100-new-members/|publisher=[[National Academy of Medicine]]|title=National Academy of Medicine Elects 100 New Members|work=National Academy of Medicine |date=21 October 2019|accessdate=3 December 2019 |last1=Lewis |first1=Talia }}</ref> and a foreign member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_5030259 |title=2019年中科院院士增选结果揭晓，64人当选 |date=22 November 2019 |work=The Paper |accessdate=22 November 2019}}</ref>
